title: import module
goal: In this lesson you will learn the import module statement to load a toolbox.
learn: Write import math or import random
Know the module name is ready to use
idea: Load a module with import math or import random. Put imports near the top of the file. After that line runs, the module name is available. Next lesson you will call tools with a dot.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, add a third print that says Modules ready. Press Run.

practice.text: Import math. Print a short message that math is ready.
practice.hint: Keep import math on top. On the next line, print() a short sentence that mentions math is ready.
practice.starterTip: Try: print("math is ready") right under import math.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if import math is present and a message prints.

practice.text: Import both math and random. Print ok.
practice.hint: Fill the two blank lines under the comment with import math and import random. One per line.
practice.starterTip: Line 2: import math. Line 3: import random. The print("ok") at the bottom can stay as-is.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if both modules imported and ok prints.

quiz.question: Which line imports the math module?
Where do imports usually go?

options.text: Near the top of the file

quiz.correct: Top of file is the common style.

quiz.question: Does import run tools by itself?

options.text: No. It loads them for later use

quiz.correct: Import prepares tools; you call them next.

project.title: Load Two Toolboxes
project.desc: Import math and random. Print a labeled line for each confirming it loaded (you may print the module or a short note).
project.starter:
import math
import random
print()
print()
